exposure: Family medicine (FM) physician presence on labor and delivery
Obstetrician (OB) presence on labor and delivery
Both FM and OB disciplines' presence on labor and delivery (hospital type: FM-only, OB-only, or Both)
outcome: unit norms supportive of vaginal birth
cohort: The study participants were 849 clinicians (physicians, nurses, and midwives) from 39 Iowa hospitals providing intrapartum care.
finding: Birthing hospitals staffed exclusively by family medicine physicians were associated with a 34.3% lower risk of cesarean delivery (among hospitals with <1,000 annual births) and stronger nursing-rated safety culture compared to hospitals with both FM and OB physicians.
mod_finding: FM-only hospitals had a lower risk of cesarean delivery, and nurses at these hospitals endorsed unit norms more supportive of vaginal birth.
